model_annotation:
Panel (a) illustrates how measured inference time varies with batch size for three 1B-parameter model variants shown as grouped vertical bar series. The x-axis is labeled “Batch size” on a linear scale, with discrete tick labels at 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 300. The y-axis is labeled “Inference time (seconds)” on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to about 11 seconds with labeled ticks at regular 2-second intervals (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10). The blue series (Llama‑1B) uses solid-filled bars and increases across the batch sizes, from a little above 3 seconds at batch size 1 to just under 11 seconds at batch size 300, with intermediate heights around the mid–3 second range at batch sizes 16–64, around the mid–5 second range at 128, and around the 9–10 second range at 256. The orange series (Lamba‑1B) uses solid-filled bars and also rises with batch size, starting just under 1 second at batch size 1 and reaching around 3 seconds by batch size 300, with intermediate bars around ~1–2.5 seconds across batch sizes 16–256. The red series (MambaInLlama‑1B) uses solid-filled bars and similarly increases, beginning slightly below 1 second at batch size 1 and rising to just under 3 seconds at batch size 300, with intermediate values around ~1–2.5 seconds across batch sizes 16–256; each batch-size group also includes a small black speedup annotation (e.g., “×3.6”, “×3.3”, “×3.1”, “×2.8”, “×3.2”, “×3.7”, “×3.7”) placed near the bars.

Panel (b) illustrates how measured inference time varies with batch size for three 3B-parameter model variants, again shown as grouped vertical bar series. The x-axis is labeled “Batch size” on a linear scale, with discrete tick labels at 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512. The y-axis is labeled “Inference time (seconds)” on a linear scale, spanning 0 to 30 seconds with labeled ticks at regular 10-second intervals (0, 10, 20, 30). The blue series (Llama‑3B) uses solid-filled bars and increases from roughly 5 seconds at batch size 1 to nearly 30 seconds at batch size 256, with intermediate bar heights around ~6–9 seconds at batch sizes 16–64 and around the mid–teens at 128; at batch size 512, there is no blue bar and the plot shows an “OOM” label at that position. The orange series (Lamba‑3B) uses solid-filled bars and rises from around 2 seconds at batch size 1 to roughly the low teens by batch size 512, with intermediate values around ~2–4 seconds at batch sizes 16–128 and around ~7 seconds at 256; at batch size 512 the orange bar is present. The red series (MambaInLlama‑3B) uses solid-filled bars and increases from around 2 seconds at batch size 1 to roughly 11–12 seconds at batch size 512, with intermediate values around ~2–4 seconds at batch sizes 16–128 and around ~5–6 seconds at 256; each batch-size group also includes a small black speedup annotation (e.g., “×2.6”, “×2.6”, “×2.3”, “×2.9”, “×3.7”, “×4.2”) placed near the bars, and an “OOM” label is shown at the 512 position for the blue series.
